doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Getting the call to tour with Miles Davis in April 1963
summary: Betty Carter's Birdland weeks, Prophet and Joe Griffin pushed him for Miles, who auditioned him at Birdland and hired him at 250 dollars.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Well you did the thing with Miles.

In ’63, before Herbie Hancock. Only a few people know about that. April 1963. And we had a great time too. See here again, Miles used to be from Chicago with them, ‘cause I’ve never pursued a gig, see I never called up a guy and said, “Hey man, give me a gig,” because that’s never been my thing, even before I could put two notes together I always said that if you could play, if you’ve got, somebody will hear. So when I went out of town I was out with Roy Haynes’ quartet. Roy Haynes, Larry Wood Ridley, Frank Strozier. So I came back. So I’d been on staff. So I said well let me get these two weeks I

got at Birdland. So somebody called and said, “You ain’t got no two weeks.” So I got up and my wife said, “Oh by the way call Betty Carter, she’s got two weeks for you at Birdland.” I was just, it was maybe five years, I don’t know. So she said also, “Do you know somebody named Prophet?” Well Prophet, his name was Richard Jennings, he was a well talented artist, he could draw pictures and paintings with birds, and Miles loved him and everybody knew him. And he knew I could comp. And Joe Griffin knew I could comp. So I called Prophet and he said, “Call Miles, Miles is getting ready to start a new band because the present band he had had just broken up, which was Wynton Kelly, Paul Chambers, J.J., Sonny Stitt was in Philadelphia, and that was the last gig. So Miles had this west coast trip. So I called him up and I said, “Hey Miles, it’s Harold.” [whispers] “How you doin’ man?” He knew who I was, “What’s happening?” I said, “Nothing, what’s goin’ on?” “I got this little tour, I want to see if you want to make it.” I said, “well yeah I’d like to” so I said — he said, “well what you doin?” I said, “I’m down at Birdland with Betty Carter Saturday night.” “I’ll be by.” I said, “What’s the money talking about?” I know what the going rate then, ‘cause I knew Cannonball was paying two-fifty. That was a lot of money. I said, “What’s the money talking about?” “What you want?” I said, “Can I get two-fifty?” “You got it.” But even then, before he was going to really hire me, he wanted to check me out just to be sure. And he said he had called everybody but me and another piano player, and I won’t call his name out of respect, and I was next to the last on the list on the list. I didn’t have no problem with that. Hey I don’t — because you know during that time I wasn’t think about working with Miles anyway. I wanted to work with Max Roach and Clifford Brown. Because remember when I came to New York, Booker Little and George Coleman was working with Max and they were getting ready to go to Philly so they didn’t have no piano. Ray Draper and Art Davis. So I go into Max and started playing the piano kind of like to let them know I knew the music. And they said, “Yeah it sounds good but there is nothing happening here so we ain’t using no piano. So Miles came down and I told Betty Carter that my closing, or her closing night would have been my opening night at the Black Hawk in San Francisco. And Benny Carter said, “I’m not going to let you out because if he wants you now he can wait a night.” So as it turns out Victor Feldman did the opening night. So Miles came by to see me at Birdland and he listened and listened. And it’s mainly because of the way I comp. The Prophet and Joe Griffith thought I would be good for Miles because I knew how to comp and stay out of his way. So I came off the bandstand and he would throw a punch at me [inaudible] he would throw a punch at me. That meant you were okay. You know, that meant I like what I’m hearing so he called me and told me where to pick up the tickets.
